checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Semifield, linear order and strict ordered-ring laws; no completeness premise
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Use established Q field/order interfaces, explain 2>0 and nonzero denominator; this is internal density of Q, not density in an already existing real line.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Strict a<b equivalent to each midpoint inequality in preceding ordered-semifield context
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Independently derive m−a=(b−a)/2 and b−m=(b−a)/2 from prior rational laws.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Midpoint gives a point strictly between ordered endpoints
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Do not import topology, real continuity or completions.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: For any x and positive y there is natural n with x≤n•y
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book derives a strict positive-natural bound for each rational record first, then scaled and reciprocal consequences; not an assumed class.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Field, linear order, strict ordered-ring laws. Rational instance uses rational ceiling in the intermediary implication
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book does not import floor/ceiling: x=[a,b], b>0, use integer M=|a|+1 and its positive natural preimage. Check b≥1, A≤Ab and strict Ab<Mb.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Positive epsilon; ordered semifield with Archimedean instance; denominator n+1
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book proves 0<1/eta(n)<epsilon with n positive. May choose different natural indexing; no sequence or limit conclusion.

checked_source_locators.locator: upper bound, least upper bound, uniqueness
checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Definitions relative to an ordered ambient set; existence not automatic
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: State ambient Q, distinguish maximum from supremum, prove uniqueness and examples. Empty set and Q have no Q supremum.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Least-upper-bound property applies only to nonempty bounded-above subsets
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book must prove it for constructed cuts after defining order; cannot use this property for Q.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Real-number Archimedean property is proved by assuming an R supremum of N if N is bounded; density statement is Q dense in R
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Do not copy this route: it would assume the later completeness construction. Book instead proves only intrinsic Q density and explicit rational-record bounds.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Nonempty bounded-above rational lower set; sup_R A not in A; ambient R already constructed; characterization A={q∈Q:q<y}
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Comparison source, not construction premise. Book defines nonempty proper lower set with no maximum without mentioning sup_R. For a lower subset of Q, properness is equivalent to a rational upper bound; under already-complete R, sup_R A∉A is equivalent to no maximum. These translations require proof, not silent substitution.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: PartialOrder suffices to identify weak-lower closure with strict-lower closure via equality case
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book uses q<a; explain equality case when comparing with library IsLowerSet.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Underlying type linearly ordered; both subsets lower; no real-number completeness
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book prove using a∈A and a∉B then every b∈B is below a. Arbitrary subsets are not comparable. Nonempty/proper/no-max needed for cuts elsewhere, not for this lemma.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Every member lower; closure of arbitrary union needs no nonempty/bounded restriction for all lower sets
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: For restricted cuts additionally prove nonempty from one member, proper from a common upper cut, and no maximum from the same witness member.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: ALL lower sets are included, including empty and full sets; supremum defined by union
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Not the same type as book cuts. Book proves union is a cut only for nonempty bounded families, then upper-bound and minimality separately. Do not call cut order a complete lattice.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Membership in supremum is existence of a member lower set containing the element
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book forms V={q∈Q:∃A∈F,q∈A} via adopted conditional subsets. This does not require a simultaneous choice function.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: LinearOrder on carrier; complete lattice includes bottom empty and top full
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book proves no global least/greatest cut and excludes empty/unbounded families; do not import library CompleteLinearOrder label.

checked_source_locators.locator: Part II preface footnote identifying earlier memoir
checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Author refers to Continuity and Irrational Numbers, Braunschweig, 1872; translated earlier in this volume
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Permitted short factual sentence: 戴德金在1872年的《连续性与无理数》中以有理数的分割讨论连续性与无理数。 Follow with this book uses a modern one-sided lower-set presentation; no claim to reproduce historical wording.

checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Preface date is not the 2007 ebook release date
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Keep historical work date, translation/digital edition and retrieval time separate.

checked_source_locators.locator: Part I section IV Creation of Irrational Numbers
checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Two classes with each first-class rational below each second-class rational; rational endpoint may belong to either side; two versions not regarded essentially different
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: Book canonically chooses lower side with no maximum and complement may have minimum. Historical source is not literally the four-condition modern definition.

checked_source_locators.locator: Part I section IV nonsquare positive integer D example
checked_source_locators.source_conditions: Uses y=x(x²+3D)/(3x²+D) for positive x; shows both sides improve; separately uses descent to show D has no rational square root
checked_source_locators.book_obligation_or_difference: This is NOT book f(q)=(2q+2)/(q+2). Book f on q≥0 and two identities independently derive from prior rational arithmetic; do not attribute its exact formula to Dedekind. Book uses already-proved non-square 2, no new general nonsquare-integer theorem or descent route.

prerequisite_content_notes: Read fun-sets plus its adopted-background preamble: finite sets, existing number sets, products, conditional subsets; no blanket powerset grant. Earlier integers/rationals allow specified equivalence-class families, so do not say no set families existed previously.
Read int-embedding and int-order-laws: injectivity in I3, order compatibility and every nonnegative integer has natural preimage at the end of I9.
Read idiv-absolute and SQ1 / non-square 2 sections; SQ anchors exist in formal batch20 manuscripts. Their file hashes bind inspected text, not root final acceptance status.

algebra_spotcheck.method: SymPy exact polynomial expansion of both cleared-denominator residuals
algebra_spotcheck.domain_conditions_separately_audited: q≥0⇒q+2>0 and (q+2)²>0; positivity of f must also be proved
algebra_spotcheck.limits: Not a Lean proof, universal program verification or manuscript acceptance

book_proof_obligations: QG1: midpoint differences, denominator 2 positive; q±1 show no endpoints, a separate quantified property.
QG1: rational record b>0 gives b≥1 using integer/natural order compatibility; M=|a|+1 has a positive natural preimage; a≤|a|≤|a|b<Mb. Apply same M to −a for two-sided bound. Do not use completeness.
QG1: eta order preservation must be composition of integer and rational embedding order laws, not inferred from injectivity. Reciprocal and scaled consequences require positive multipliers.
QG2: relative upper-bound/supremum definitions, uniqueness, maximum iff attained supremum, {q<1} counterexample to no-maximum⇒no-supremum; empty and whole Q cases.
QG3: domain q≥0; q+2>0, numerator 2q+2>0. Expand both identities explicitly. f is not a total function on all Q: q=−2 is excluded.

QG3/QG4: S={q≥0:q²<2} nonempty (0,1), bounded by 2; every upper bound u≥1. Exclude u²<2 using a larger S member, u²=2 by prior SQ4 consequence; u²>2 yields a smaller POSITIVE upper bound, verified against arbitrary s∈S by nonnegative square order reflection.
DC1: openly adopt P(Q) existence and conditional subset formation. Previous fun-sets alone did not assert the full powerset. R_cut is a subset of P(Q); no unrestricted all-objects set.
DC1: nonempty proper downward closed no-maximum definition. Check four conditions for i(r)={q<r}; complement may have minimum r. Do not use {q≤r}.

DC2: prove inclusion reflexive/transitive/antisymmetric and comparability of lower sets; prove i preserves AND reflects ≤, strict < and equality. Only order embedding, no arithmetic structure on cuts.
DC2: witness a∈A gives i(a) properly below A; b∉A gives A properly below i(b+1). No global bottom or top.
DC3: S is not a cut, since 0∈S but −1∉S. D adds all negatives. Check lower closure and no-max separately for negative/nonnegative inputs; same-square order applies only nonnegative.
DC3: prove D={q:∃s∈S,q<s}; D=i(r) would make r the Q supremum of S via order reflection. Do not write D²=i(2) or assign sqrt_Q(2).
DC4: given nonempty F and common upper cut U, V={q∈Q:∃A∈F,q∈A} is nonempty/proper/lower/no-max. Give one witness at a time, no choice function.

DC4: separate common-upper-bound and leastness proofs. Empty union fails nonempty; union of all i(q) is Q and fails properness, and this family has no cut upper bound. Only conditional order completeness.
DC4: F_S={i(s):s∈S} is nonempty bounded by i(2); its union D is its cut-order supremum, compatible with no Q supremum for S.

All eight groups require original full manuscript/answer proofs later. No real arithmetic, ordered-field claim for cuts, real-root existence, convergence, topology or general cut decision API is established by this source audit.
